verdict.rationale: Warp's open-source announcement says it is shipping a settings file that gives programmatic control over settings and easy portability between devices. That directly targets plain-text, dotfile-style config. However, the only evidence is a single blog statement, with no reference docs on file format, location, or scope. missing for 10: documentation of the settings file format and location, evidence that it covers the full configuration (themes, keybindings, prompts, etc.), confirmation it works in a dotfiles/sync workflow, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can keep the terminal's full configuration as plain-text files in my dotfiles and sync it across machines

citations.quote: we are shipping a (long-overdue) settings file so that users and agents get programmatic control over settings and easy portability between devices.
